BudgetUsage.description:
Usage counters. `model_calls` counts calls that returned a usable response; `model_attempts` every request
sent (incl. failures and lost responses); tokens are only what the provider reported — calls without usage data
are counted in `unreported_calls`, calls whose response was lost in `unconfirmed_calls`.
BudgetUsage.title: BudgetUsage

max_steps.description: maximum path length explored (0 for single-step queries)

ConditionCheck.description: One business / resource condition evaluated by an execution gate.

holds.description: None: the gate could not determine it
holds.title: Holds

ConditionCheck.title: ConditionCheck

ConflictInfo.description: Why a proposal based on an older world revision was rejected (shared-resource arbitration).
ConflictInfo.title: ConflictInfo

domain.description: enum or entity set of a symbolic value; required when ambiguous
domain.title: Domain

CostTerm.description:
One additive cost term of an objective level.

- action_cost: `weight` × the declared `cost` of every action taken on the path.
- state_rate: `weight` × `expr` (int) evaluated on every post-state s_1..s_k of the path.
- terminal: `weight` × `expr` (int) evaluated on the final state s_k of the path.
CostTerm.title: CostTerm

expected_by.description: what produced the expectation, e.g. model:<package>@<version>
expected_by.title: Expected By

EvidenceRef.description: Reference to something that supports a claim: an event, artifact, check or snapshot.
EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

ExecutionContext.description:
The authoritative basis of one send, built by the kernel right before it (phase 4A, A2) — never by a strategy.

Identity comes from the kernel's turn (not the proposal's `actor_id` claim), the environment / session / service
identity from the run's environment, and `current_revision` from the environment's own authoritative read at the
side-effect boundary. `proposal_revision` is kept separately: the revision the plan was made on is not the
revision the write happens on. When the current revision cannot be read it is None with `revision_source`
UNKNOWN, and a gate that needs it must deny. Receipts bind to `execution_binding(context)` — the same canonical
form is used to issue and to verify.

actor_id.description: the actor of the kernel's turn (authoritative identity)
actor_id.title: Actor Id

current_revision.description: the environment's revision at the send
current_revision.title: Current Revision

proposal_revision.description: the revision the proposal was planned on
proposal_revision.title: Proposal Revision

revision_source.description: FRESH: read from the environment right before the send (env.current_revision); SERIALIZED: a pure-data environment whose state lives in this serialized step; UNKNOWN: could not be read
revision_source.title: Revision Source

versions.description: model, driver/adapter, rules, participant view, environment and gate versions
versions.title: Versions

ExecutionContext.title: ExecutionContext

ExecutionDecision.description:
Typed record of one pre-execution decision (phase 3A, G2): kept on the operation record and as an event, so
decision, operation record and the backend's side effect can be traced to each other.

execution.description: the basis the decision was made on (phase 4A); absent in older records

ExecutionDecision.title: ExecutionDecision

ExecutionPhase.description: Which kind of send a pre-execution decision is about (phase 3A, G2).
ExecutionPhase.title: ExecutionPhase

Extension.description: Namespaced, versioned extension payload. `schema_id` names the JSON Schema that validates `data`.
Extension.title: Extension

evidence.description: basis of `observed`: fresh observation, verified within a stated scope (probe / operation query), or unknown (not comparable); `predicted` marks a value only the model supplies (v2)
evidence.title: Evidence

ModelUsage.description: Model usage of one proposal: `model_calls` usable responses, `attempts` requests sent; tokens as reported.
ModelUsage.title: ModelUsage

proven_lower.description: no plan within the horizon is cheaper than this
proven_lower.title: Proven Lower

proven_upper.description: a plan at most this expensive exists
proven_upper.title: Proven Upper

value.description: objective value of the returned plan
value.title: Value

ObjectiveLevel.description: One lexicographic level: minimise (or maximise) the sum of its terms over the path.
ObjectiveLevel.title: ObjectiveLevel

ObjectiveSpec.description:
What a cost-aware planner optimises (P2-020).

A candidate plan is a path s_0 → … → s_k (k ≤ horizon) that ends in the first state where `goal_property`
holds. Its value on each level is the sum of the level's terms over that path (see `CostTerm`); levels are
compared lexicographically in list order. Costs stop accumulating once the goal holds.
ObjectiveSpec.title: ObjectiveSpec

requested_paths.description: locations observed fresh on request (OBSERVE_MORE, v2)
requested_paths.title: Requested Paths

semantics.default: Facts are what the actor observed (possibly stale, see observed_at_step); unknowns are locations whose current value the actor cannot know at this step. The environment truth state is a separate object that agents never receive.
semantics.title: Semantics

step.description: logical step at which the observation is taken
step.title: Step

turn.description: turn the observation was taken for (v2)

for_action.description: ground action key the request is about

ObservationRequest.title: ObservationRequest

ParticipantView.description:
What one participant's planner receives (phase 3A, G4): observed values of locations outside the view are
withheld before its belief is built (they count as never observed), and settings are read from its own map
first. The planner never sees the withheld values; the environment and the kernel still work on the truth.

include.description: location families or paths the planner may see (empty = every location)

settings.description: participant settings, read before the platform settings

source.title: Source
